en: When PAGASA announces a heat index above 42 degrees Celsius, avoid outdoor play to prevent dangerous heatstroke.
During an earthquake, immediately drop to the ground, take cover under a sturdy table, and hold on until the shaking stops.
Avoid wading in floodwaters because they often contain rat urine carrying leptospirosis, a severe bacterial infection.
Never look directly at a solar eclipse without certified eclipse glasses, as the sun's rays can permanently blind you.
Always check the tide schedule before beach swimming, because spring tides during a full moon bring dangerously strong rip currents.
If you hear thunder during a storm, immediately go indoors because lightning can strike up to 16 kilometers away.
Always wash root crops like camote grown in soil thoroughly to remove harmful parasites before eating.
Wear a mask when cutting or sanding rocks to prevent inhaling microscopic silica dust that severely damages your lungs.
Evacuate immediately if you notice new cracks in the soil or tilting trees, as these indicate an impending landslide.
Apply broad-spectrum sunscreen before outdoor recess to block harmful ultraviolet rays from the sun that cause painful sunburns.
Store at least three days of drinking water and non-perishable food before a typhoon to survive potential power outages.
If lost at night, locate the North Star to determine true north and safely navigate your way back home.
